Either singly or in large communal caravans, Wanderer Gnomes roam all over Mennara as traders, performers, and occasionally even laborers in local farms and smithies, a common sight throughout the land. Sources Gnomes (Character Species), p. 69

title: Wanderer's Stone
content: Wanderer's Stone Wanderer's stones are worn on the chest and direct an emanation of healing energy to the heart and lungs. While this energy is too subtle to help heal injuries or disease, it does effectively stave off the effects of fatigue. Characters who bear one of these shards are able to walk, run, swim, row, fly, and fight with significantly improved stamina. Often, instead of using their shards themselves, bearers attach them to the harness of a mount or draft animal in their possession. Sources Runebound Shards (Call to Adventure), p. 121

title: War of the Shadow Tear
content: War of the Shadow Tear The War of the Shadow Tear is a calamity of the past to which some Corrupted Lands elsewhere in Mennara — regions where the boundary to the Ynfernael runs thin, beyond the Darklands of The Ru — may date back. [not stated in source: further detail on the war itself] Sources Whispers of the Ynfernael (The Ru Steppes and Beyond), p. 219

title: Warding Talisman
content: Warding Talisman Warding Talismans have a form and appearance similar to beautifully crafted silver ailettes: small badges in the shape of shields worn on the upper chest or shoulder. They don't offer much physical protection, but they carry enchantments that can cause an opponent's strike to falter or go awry. Sources Magic Items, p. 111

title: Warlord Hellspanth
content: Warlord Hellspanth Warlord Hellspanth led a band of dragons from the far north who allied with Llovar during the First Darkness, the first time the people of Terrinoth faced dragons in battle — though lacking in numbers, Hellspanth's drakes proved deadly foes. After the Orcs of Chief Lukosh deserted the Ynfernael cause, Llovar could rely only upon Hellspanth's dragons as powerful allies for the remainder of the war. Hellspanth's ultimate fate, like those of Llovar's other allies, is not recorded in any scrolls to be found. Sources The First Darkness (Tales of Darkness), pp. 35, 37 The Third Darkness (Tales of Darkness), p. 45

title: Warriors' Guild
content: Warriors' Guild The Warriors' Guild is one of the Dunwarr Guilds, standing ready to protect all of the Dunwarr Deeps against any threat. In Thelgrim, the Guild maintains two barracks, one abutting each of the city's main gate complexes: the southern barracks, commanded by Skirmisher Captain Lyssa Svensdottir, oversee all military action outside the mountains, while the northern barracks, commanded by her brother Guard Captain Einalf Svensson, oversee the defense of the Deeps and the Palace Guard protecting King Geirmund Ragnarson. Together with the Rangers' Guild, the Warriors' Guild is also tasked with exterminating the kobold packs that infest the Dunwarr Mountains, a duty that typically falls to its newest members. Sources Duldor Deeps (The Dunwarr Mountains), p. 189 Thelgrim (The Dunwarr Mountains), p. 187

title: Watchers
content: Watchers The Watchers are a special order within the priests of Aris who guard the Weeping Basin to ensure the Dragonlord Margath, said to have fallen there after being slain, never rises again. Sources Spirits of Power (The Strength of Devotion), p. 123

title: Wavedancer
content: Wavedancer The Wavedancer was the sturdy vessel Lathina Veintralla and Keiren O'Brallen commissioned in Dallak to sail west into the sunset in search of long-forgotten lands. Presumed lost after years without word, the Wavedancer returned to port five years later, less one of its masts and half its crew, having reached the distant shores of Zanaga and the Sunderlands. Sources The Age of Courage (Tales of Darkness), p. 53

title: Wealdworker
content: Wealdworker The Wealdworkers, also called Wealdweavers or Wealdcallers in some sources, are an order of the Latari with sanctums in the sacred vales of Lithelin. The cults of the Wealdweavers tend the waters of The Fountain of Purity and the Aymhelin saplings nourished by them. [not stated in source: the reason for the name variance between "Wealdworkers," "Wealdweavers," and "Wealdcallers"] Description The ancient songs of the Latari comforted them when they first fell to Mennara, but they did not expect their lays to awaken the very forest itself: the voices of the Elves stirred some unknown joy in the mysterious hearts of the young forest, giving movement to the roots and boughs and trunks of the wood. The very first Finwalyn, or forest children, were awakened this way, and the Elves learned that they had perhaps been granted some sway over the sphere of life after all. Since then, the Wealdcallers have learned to sing and speak to the plants and trees of the forest and bid them grow in specific directions, allowing the Elves to build their cities in relative harmony with the natural landscape. On rare occasions, the Elves will call up the very forest floor to aid them in their fight against the enemy, unleashing heather and thorn and vine and branch against those who would dare trespass in their emerald haven. In the aftermath of such battles, the powers of the Wealdcallers have also allowed the Elves to heal parts of the Aymhelin where fire or corruption have taken hold, returning the plant life there to its original verdant state. To outsiders, the magic of the Wealdcallers is reminiscent of both spiritspeaking and the bardic magic of certain music. When asked about the similarities, and the true source of their power, the Elves answer with only a mysterious, plaintive melody. Sources Lithelin and the Ailatar (The Aymhelin), p. 175 The Deepwood (The Aymhelin), p. 177 Wealdcallers (Elven Magic), p. 129

title: Weeping Basin
content: Weeping Basin The Weeping Basin in Terrinoth is a crater lake said to mark the spot where the body of the Dragonlord Margath fell to earth after being slain by Baron Rolan, and site of Aris's largest shrine. Whispers speak of the Watchers, a special order within the priests of Aris who guard the lake to ensure Margath never rises again; some say those who visit the crater lake and drink of its waters receive the strength and vigor of Aris herself, but only if they truly need it. [not stated in source: this account conflicts with the Tales of Darkness history of Margath's death, which holds that Lord Roland of Kell slew Margath in the Mountains of Despair near Kell and that neither rider's remains were ever recovered from the snow-shrouded peaks — see Margath and Roland of Kell. Both accounts are recorded as-is; the sources do not reconcile them.] Sources Spirits of Power (The Strength of Devotion), p. 123

title: Weeping Causeway
content: Weeping Causeway The Weeping Causeway was built by a Sephone ancestor as a memorial to his slain father, and has long served as the mustering ground for the combined armies of Allerfeldt. Sources Western Terrinoth (Terrinoth), p. 142

title: Weik Warrior
content: Weik Warrior The rugged peoples of the north are as fearsome as the land they call home. Weik warriors stride into battle with a blade or axe in each hand, wild grins upon their faces — for in the culture of the Weik, there can be no greater honor than to die by the sword. Cold and hardship mean little to them, and they look upon the Human knights and soldiers of Terrinoth as weakling southerners; some Weik even travel to these warmer lands in search of greater adventure or to hunt a foe who dares think they can escape the wrath of a Weik who has been wronged. Heroes dealing with the Hearthlords will almost certainly find themselves interacting with Weik warriors as well, either to earn their trust with shows of martial skill, or to join their hunting parties as they seek out the ice-blood creatures of Isheim. Sources Life in the Cold (Isheim), p. 239

title: Weik
content: Weik The Weik are the rugged peoples of the north who have carved out a civilization on the shores of Isheim along The Raider's Coast, winning a reputation as daring seafarers, skilled game hunters, and deadly raiders. Table of Contents History Society Sources History The history of the Hearthlords reaches back to that time when the first Weik dragged their longships onto Isheim's shores. In those days, the people of the Weik's twelve pirate fleets were nomads and hunters on the open seas, and they had grown too numerous for their island hideaways and open-ocean flotilla towns. When Lagrul the Red spied the snowcapped Isheim coast, he proclaimed the spot the last port, and turned his fleet for its cliffs. Several hundred years later, cities and towns mark the Weik's landing sites, and the Hearthlords hold the title of jarl, handed down from the first captains. Society Weik warriors stride into battle with a blade or axe in each hand, wild grins upon their faces — for in the culture of the Weik, there can be no greater honor than to die by the sword. Cold and hardship mean little to them, and they look upon the Human knights and soldiers of Terrinoth as weakling southerners; some Weik even travel to these warmer lands in search of greater adventure or to hunt a foe who dares think they can escape the wrath of a Weik who has been wronged. More importantly than acting as rulers, the Hearthlords also serve as the embodiment of the Weik's endless struggle against the brutal environment of Isheim and their war against Nordros, the icy God of Cold and Death. It is each Hearthlord's duty to dig the roots of their city deeper into the soil of Isheim than their predecessor, clearing its forests, harvesting its wildlife, and raising new settlements. The success of these cities has led to a new problem for the Weik: trade wars over exotic goods coveted by southern lands, especially ice-blood, the vital fluids of rare northern creatures like the wendigo and the ice wyrms. Sources The Frozen North (Isheim), pp. 232–233 Lords of the Hearth (Isheim), p. 234 Life in the Cold (Isheim), p. 239

title: Well of Sins
content: Well of Sins The Well of Sins is a tangle of fallen bridges deep within the Gyrar Abyss, hidden in the cool shadows of its chasm cities, where the Uthuk come to trade slaves and souls. Sources Tribes of the Uthuk Y'llan (The Ru Steppes and Beyond), p. 211

title: Wendigo
content: Wendigo Wendigo are creations of the Rime Storm. According to the tales, they were once the feline mounts of the Salishwyrd, back when the north encompassed green forests and open plains — then the Rime Storm infected them with icy magic. Their eyes shrank away to nothing, and a hunger as keen as the howling tundra wind filled their bellies. It was not long before they became a terror of the north, their chilling cries sending sensible creatures scurrying for their dens and wise individuals reaching for their weapons. Eyeless, these creatures bite the air to gain a sense of their prey; they can pinpoint a target's location far swifter than the keenest of hunters. Many wendigo are servants of the Ice Wyrms, as a frigid arcane link binds each together — the wyrms use these terrible beasts as trackers and assassins that seek out intruders into their realm, skulking among the shadows and serving as guard dogs for ice wyrm lairs. Ice-Blood Warrior clans might fight alongside wendigo, though the warriors have little control over their savage allies. Many wild wendigo also inhabit the north, fiercely territorial, and an expedition might wander into their hunting grounds without realizing it — at least until the beasts start stalking them and picking off their members one by one. In the Thorn Vales, beings of iced blood worship wendigo as gods. Sources Life in the Cold (Isheim), pp. 238–239 Realm of the White Death (Isheim), p. 236

title: Whispering Forest
content: Whispering Forest The Whispering Forest lies to the east of Dhernas in Eastern Terrinoth, a heavily forested, largely unsettled territory surrounded by many dark rumors; nearby communities nonetheless rely on it for game and timber. Sources Eastern Terrinoth (Terrinoth), p. 138

title: Whispermen
content: Whispermen The Whispermen are ragged descendants of the lost expedition into Zanaga who dwell in the Chasm of Despair, gouging out their own eyes so they might forever dwell in darkness, an offering to their midnight god Var Ni. Stories tell of how the Whispermen have been building tunnels under all of Zanaga for long years now, awaiting the day when their master puts out the hated sun and they might rise up and slaughter all who are not natives of the night. It was the Whispermen who unearthed Var Ni's vast remains, and it is they who pour the blood of their sacrifices into his fanged maw; even in his inert state, the bat god sends out vile dreams and squalls of darkness across the land, causing shamans to mumble of the coming night and whole regions to suddenly plunge into darkness, and it is within this supernatural darkness that the Whispermen do their work, slowly paving the way for Var Ni's return. Sources The Lost Expedition (Zanaga), p. 255

title: Winged Boots
content: Winged Boots The Priesthood of Pollux sponsors all manner of magical research into artifacts that might allow their wearer to fly. Winged Boots are an example of such endeavors, but even so, they do not enable soaring flight. An adventurer equipped with winged boots can hover a few dozen yards above the ground or use the boots to safely slow a descent from a height. When not worn, Winged Boots have a tendency to spring upwards and fly away on their own. Sources Magic Items, p. 111

title: Wintersmeet
content: Wintersmeet Wintersmeet is the Rangers' Guild's traditional week of feasting and fellowship, held during the depths of winter at the solstice. Rangers of The Northern Coast and the rest of The Frontier, who otherwise often go months without seeing another Dwarf, try each year to make the trek to Hadranhold to take part. Sources The Frontier (The Dunwarr Mountains), p. 190

title: Witch and Warlock (Uthuk)
content: Witch and Warlock (Uthuk) Witches and warlocks are the spiritual slave masters of the Uthuk tribes and the keepers of their dark Ynfernael magic. Only a handful of Uthuk are born with such gifts; these children often arrive into the world amid a portentous rain of blood or storm of crimson lightning. A long and torturous road follows their birth, and not all of them live to master their magic, as the brutality of Uthuk society ruthlessly weeds out the weak. Those who survive are cruel and skilled sorcerers and priestesses, utterly dedicated to the Uthuk and without a shred of mercy for their enemies. Most common among their kind are the bloodwitches, for whom the cardinal fluids of the body are theirs to command — a bloodwitch can hear the blood of her enemies as it pumps through their veins and read the future by gazing into the crimson torrent of a fresh-made wound, and with a gesture can spark a person's heart aflame, setting their blood to boiling until it bursts forth from their screaming mouth. In contrast, warlocks of the Uthuk are masters of dark dreams, traveling the Aenlong as they sleep, hunting foes, speaking with demons, and summoning horrors into the world. Kin to bloodwitches, bonewitches manipulate skeletons, often while they are encased in living flesh — foes can find their limbs snapped like twigs, while allies can be hardened against harm, the witch thickening ribs and skulls to ward away blows. Revered leaders among their kind, both witches and warlocks are able to communicate telepathically with other Uthuk across vast distances. These links bind the Uthuk tribes together and are used to call their armies to battle, bringing both berserkers and warlords alike to heel with but a hateful glance. The greatest among them rise to become bloodsisters and nightseers. Sources Life in the Ru (The Ru Steppes and Beyond), p. 217

title: Wizard's Vale
content: Wizard's Vale The Wizard's Vale is the remote valley where Timmorran built the Tower of Meringyr for his magical research, and where he was slain by Waiqar on the Night of Betrayal in 515. As Waiqar uttered his terrible oath to hunt down every fragment of the shattered Orb of the Sky, he summoned into being a great tempest that lashed the Vale with freezing and poisonous rain; the lives of those who stood within sight of Meringyr were snuffed out by the vow's utterance, becoming the first of Waiqar's Deathborn Legion. Sources The Second Darkness (Tales of Darkness), pp. 40–41

title: Wraith
content: Wraith Despite the fearsome nature of Waiqar's forces, none of them are as dreaded as wraiths. Whether they existed before the Undying One claimed The Mistlands, or are beings he created with his own arcane powers, is a matter of much debate with both peasants and wizards alike — perhaps only those who serve the Thirteenth Baron know with certainty. Several Greyhaven scholars who dare study such matters believe wraiths are the manifestations of tragic or violent deaths involving dark emotions, ones so powerful that death itself could not still the intense hate, passion, or jealousy involved; such spirits, they say, rise after the corpse falls, ghastly flowing forms far more destructive than mere shades. They especially turn their ire towards any who would disturb them as they haunt decaying deathbeds, ancient battlefields, crumbling treasure vaults, and other places that perhaps had special meaning to their lives (or deaths). These horrific spectral creatures conjure fear in even the most stouthearted of Daqan knights as they eerily glide over marshes and through bulwarks, bringing the icy cold touch of the grave to whomever they encounter; often just the sight of a single wraith is enough to send disciplined units screaming in retreat, and many an adventuring band has been reduced to a single gibbering survivor who barely returns to tell their tale. Sources Unlife in the Mists (The Mistlands), p. 167

title: Wyrm Queen
content: Wyrm Queen The Wyrm Queen is said by some to be the mother of the Dragon Hybrids who accompanied the dragonlords' invasion during the Third Darkness, creatures previously unseen in Terrinoth before that war. Some Greyhaven scholars instead hold that the hybrids are the result of cruel experimentations or forbidden magics rather than natural offspring, though that they are the spawn of dragons is clear from their form: long snouts filled with sharp teeth, snaking tails, and thick scales, in stature similar to Humans but taller and more heavily muscled, some bearing wings or fiery breath. Sources The Third Darkness (Tales of Darkness), p. 45

title: Wyrm of the Deep
content: Wyrm of the Deep Mennara is known for its many dragonkin that roam over its varied terrain. While most possess deep and ancient wisdoms, some have seemingly devolved into little more than beasts of hunger and fury. The fathomless seas that lay beyond the shores of Lorimor and The Torue Albes are home to one such strain, gigantic creatures that prey on seagoing vessels all along the western coast. Many sightings are reported even in the well-traveled southern waters separating Al-Kalim and Zanaga, a truly frightening occurrence for passengers; experienced sailors, though, know that the true terrors are the gods that also live in the seas, and would rather face a wyrm any day. While most vessels desperately seek to put as much distance as possible between a deepwyrm sighting and their own fragile vessels, others actually seek these creatures out. Wyrm hunters are a breed apart, traveling in packs aboard chartered ships or accompanying merchant ships to offer defence in case of unexpected attacks; these brave individuals have a near ancestral hatred of the wyrms, and will even leap onto the backs of the creatures to ensure they are slain, even though it invariably means their own death. The scales and organs fetch high prices in Tamalir and Al-Medena, where alchemists use them for especially potent potions. Some scholars (and pirates) firmly believe these creatures are not Dragonkin at all, but some other form of reptilian being perhaps utterly unique to the ocean depths. Those who have dared to venture into The Molten Heath or Isheim to ask the dragons directly have never returned, however. Sources Life in the West (Lorimor and the Torue Albes), pp. 231

title: Xitotl
content: Xitotl Xitotl is the sacred moon city of the Lizardmen in Zanaga; its upper levels house Humans and Mahkim, while the lizardmen live in the shadows below. Sources Tribes of the Serpent Gods (Zanaga), p. 257

title: Xor
content: Xor The Orc Xor runs the fighting pits of Last Haven, where visitors can win or lose coin, as well as perhaps some teeth. Sources Tribes of the Uthuk Y'llan (The Ru Steppes and Beyond), p. 212

title: Yeron Riders
content: Yeron Riders The Yeron Riders are a legendary flying cavalry unit based in The Thalian Glades, among the most elite group of warriors to be found anywhere in Mennara, overseen by Aishalan Finnan. Saddled upon the incredibly rare flying horses known as the Yeron, the Yeron Riders keep watch for threats near and far, protecting the glades against raids and incursions. When not patrolling, the Yeron and their riders are able to live in relative peace and prosperity, enjoying the beauty of their environs. Sources The Thalian Glades (The Aymhelin), p. 178

title: Yeron
content: Yeron The Yeron are incredibly rare flying horses native to The Aymhelin, saddled by the Yeron Riders of The Thalian Glades to keep watch for threats near and far. Lord Roland of Kell rode a winged Yeron into the air during the climactic battle of the Third Darkness, using it to summon freezing rain onto the dragonlord Margath's position with an ice storm runebound shard before driving his lance through the great drake's neck; Margath broke the wings of Roland's mount in his death throes, and both riders fell to their deaths, their remains never recovered. [not stated in source: whether this Yeron came from the Thalian Glades unit] Sources The Thalian Glades (The Aymhelin), p. 178 The Third Darkness (Tales of Darkness), pp. 45–48

title: Ygraine Cunningham
content: Ygraine Cunningham Countess Ygraine Cunningham was a past ruler of Haverford County within Allerfeldt, remembered as one of the few Cunninghams whose obsession proved productive: her reinforced training hall for battlemages, unlike most of her line's half-finished grand projects and failed alchemical experiments. Sources Western Terrinoth (Terrinoth), p. 143

title: Ynfernael Rune
content: Ynfernael Rune Unlike most runebound shards, Ynfernael runes were not carved by the Dragonlords of the Third Darkness. Instead, they are shards that have been captured and corrupted through the malicious actions of those who seek the regard of demons. An Ynfernael rune has one purpose: to inflict pain on others. The bearer of an Ynfernael rune must spill some of their own blood to activate the shard, but once they have done so, the unholy power unleashed ensures their foes will spill an even greater amount. Sources Runebound Shards (Call to Adventure), p. 121

title: Ynfernael
content: Ynfernael The Ynfernael is a separate plane of reality made of vile, negative energy and boundless evil, existing both outside of Mennara and parallel to it like a warped mirror upon the mortal world. Table of Contents Overview Ynfernael Magic in Mennara The Signs of the Ynfernael Sources Overview Awash with unfathomable darkness, the Ynfernael is the home of unnatural creatures that emerge out of its all-encompassing rage and despair like hungry sharks leaping from roiling oceans. It is an unknowable plane of existence that is drawn to the most horrid acts of mortals, taking their offerings of blood and murder and gifting them with strength and rage in return; none can comprehend the motives of its unholy creatures, only that their actions echo the abhorrent plane of their existence. Its dread effects on Mennara across the centuries are fully evident — even the Tears of Latariana were not immune to the corruption of the Ynfernael, and mere mortals and their works even less so. The power of the Ynfernael grows everywhere, defiling all it touches, until one day it will transform all of Mennara into an unending, bloodsoaked cauldron of evil. Ynfernael Magic in Mennara Scholars in Greyhaven and elsewhere hold that despite its vile nature, the Ynfernael is a primordial part of all existence; some others simply believe it is the source of all evil in Mennara, tracing every terrible act and betrayal back to its influence on the desperate and weak-willed. They hold that where the boundary between Mennara and the Aenlong is thin and tenuous, the Ynfernael's baneful energies can spill through and befoul the land and taint those who reside there, no matter their intentions or will — regions thought to be so porous are known as Corrupted Lands, where trees become stunted and twisted into unnerving shapes, plants grow hungry for flesh, and even the most timid of creatures become feral and thirsty for blood. The Darklands are infamous for such lands, the most infamous being where Llovar first dreamwalked into the Ynfernael, though other areas in Mennara may be equally porous, perhaps dating back to the calamities of the War of the Shadow Tear or as the sites of horrid rituals. The Uthuk Y'llan fully embrace the Ynfernael, its foul energy pulsing in each beat of their hearts and each drop of blood they spill; it has been the source of their furious power ever since Llovar transformed the peaceful plains-dwellers of the Loth K'har into the Locust Swarm. As the power corrupted and transformed their flesh, it twisted the magics of the Loth K'har as well, turning their nightseers' ancient dreamwalking tradition toward communing with demons and dominating the Locust armies. Since then, the Uthuk have honed their ability to travel the Aenlong to gain glimpses of the Ynfernael plane and its inhabitants; the most powerful of these demons call on Ynfernael magic with ease, as it flows from the plane of evil and through them like blood coursing through veins. The Uthuk are not the only ones in Mennara who use Ynfernael magic — the Daewyl Elves also appear to draw on this unholy power. These Elves had dared to travel to blighted planes of the Aenlong to slay the many corrupted creatures there, but were themselves corrupted by the Ynfernael taint; many of the Daewyl now call upon that dark source of magic as they single-mindedly fight against evil, no matter the consequences to themselves or those around them. The Signs of the Ynfernael Although there are dark hints that Ynfernael magic bled into Mennara in earlier times, it was not until Llovar Rutonu that this foul practice gained a powerful foothold. Though study of such magic is utterly forbidden, some mages believe it a dark counterpart to Divine magic — as the Empyrean blesses all that is good and pure in magic, so the Ynfernael empowers that which is horrid and dark. From a forgotten rift, its influence spread across the Ru, infesting both the peoples of this land and the land itself: bodies deform as protruding talons and bone-spurs grow and spurt out of coarsened skin, and some of the corrupting energy became the fuel for fearsome magic, especially for those who became the first witches of bone and blood, their veins rich with demonic blood. Such magic is powerful but difficult to control, and many who are born with the talent to wield it destroy themselves as they seek to master the power of demons. The witches of the Blood Coven carefully oversee their progress, and weed out the weak through tortuous rites and fierce competitions; the survivors join the coven as apprentices, and once fully proven as loyal and worthy of the full blessings of the Ynfernael, they use their sorceries to both terrify and inspire the disparate tribes into a unified, unstoppable horde. Uthuk warlocks operate in even darker manners, roaming across the Aenlong in their sleep, hunting down their enemies like deer and conversing with the fell beings of the Ynfernael; it is their dealings that reveal their true dangers, for they are the masters of the dark rituals and fell ceremonies of blood and screams. Through these sacrifices, warlocks implore the Ynfernael to summon forth demons into Mennara — such conjurations can involve many weeks of vile consecrations and horrid, unceasing chants, all to allow the summoned creatures a strong presence in the mortal plane that is not easily severed. The horrid murder ceremonies the Uthuk commonly conduct before battles are more swift but allow demons only a fleeting foothold, though it is usually long enough for them to thoroughly petrify and devour enemy forces. Warlocks also eschew direct roles to wield their power secretly, growing cults of followers in western lands like Terrinoth, Lorimor, and even Al-Kalim, burrowing deeply into the soft, exposed underbelly of their foes and poisoning it with the taint of Ynfernael magic through blood rituals, often involving kidnapped inhabitants for the freshest and most powerful effect. Sources Whispers of the Ynfernael (The Ru Steppes and Beyond), pp. 218–219

title: Young Dragon
content: Young Dragon Dragons take decades, even centuries, to fully mature; unlike the wild dragons of the southern lands, the dragons of The Molten Heath are highly protective of their dragonlings, shielding them from the worst dangers of their homeland until they come of age. During this time, the elder dragons instruct the young in the history of their race, which is the history of all creation. From a young age, dragons learn of their unique place in the cosmos as the inheritors of the Yrthwrights' legacy; by the time they reach adulthood, dragons understand the weight of their role as stewards of Mennara and guardians of its inhabitants — at least, most of them do. Although weak and fragile compared to fully grown dragons, the youngest wyrmling is far from defenseless: a newly hatched dragon might be the size of a small stag, with talons strong and sharp enough to split a warrior open. Within a few years at most, the dragonling stands larger and stronger than an ox. Similarly, although they lack the intense depth of insight and centuries of wisdom of their elders, even the youngest dragons are at least the intellectual equals of the finest minds of Human civilization. Sources Life on the Heath (The Molten Heath), p. 196

title: Yrthwright's Forge
content: Yrthwright's Forge Yrthwright's Forge is a great mountain shrine west of Tamalir, at whose base the Free City of Forge is built, named as a reminder of the glory of the ancient Dwarven kingdom of the Karok Doum. Refugee Dwarves fleeing the destruction of the Karok Doum built the city of Yrthwright's Forge beside a volcano in the heart of a bountiful valley. During the Third Darkness, the city was a desirable prize for the dragons for the volcanic fires burning within the mountain's depths, which powered industry and mining and provided a habitat the dragons found comfortingly like a portion of the Molten Heath; the Dragonlord Avox led the assault on the city, enslaving its Dwarves and forcing them to dig deep into the mountains while abducting Humans from nearby villages to join them in the mines. In the aftermath, the Terrinoth noble Lady Ysbet led an army to Yrthwright's Forge and orchestrated a brilliant series of tunnel fights that ended in her slaying Avox; the freed slaves hailed her as a savior and asked her to become governor of the settlement, now envisioned as a new Free City. Sources The Early History of the Dwarves (Tales of Darkness), p. 31 The Third Darkness (Tales of Darkness), pp. 46–47 The Free Cities (Terrinoth), p. 146

title: Yrthwrights
content: Yrthwrights The Yrthwrights, also called the Foundrakes, are the first dragons and the creators of Mennara; dragons see themselves as the inheritors of the Yrthwrights' legacy, understanding their role as stewards of Mennara and guardians of its inhabitants — at least, most of them do. History The Dragonkin must have existed before The First created the mortal realm, since the Dragonkin played a part in its construction, molded from the debris of creation and granted the ability to speak matter into existence in a manner reminiscent of the Lays of the First — though Runemasters of Greyhaven disagree as to whether the runes of the dragons are vestiges of that same language. Through their incantations, the first dragons set about creating the Firma Dracem, the mortal realm, and adorned it with spinning bodies, planets, and suns; for this great work, nothing less than existence as mortals perceive it, they were termed the Foundrakes, also called the Yrthwrights. One of their number, the Yrthwright Mennara, architected the glade that became The Aymhelin and passed judgment upon the rebellious Elves who stumbled into it, exiling them to the very world that some dare name in Mennara's honor. Description A number of dragons throughout history have seen the mortals of Mennara as potentially useful tools in the battle to protect the Yrthwrights' creation from the depredations of the Ynfernael and the abyssal entities that dwell within. Sources Tales of Darkness, p. 24 The Elves (Tales of Darkness), pp. 26–27 Life on the Heath (The Molten Heath), p. 195

title: Zachareth
content: Zachareth Baron Zachareth rules Carthridge, the Silver Barony, keeping his knights and foot soldiers in a constant state of readiness despite centuries without serious challenge. Owing to Carthridge's ancient border with the Thirteenth Barony, Zachareth is the only baron who speaks regularly and emphatically of the threat posed by the Mistlands, agitating for a preemptive invasion he volunteers to lead himself. The other barons have refused to support the idea; Barons Xarles and Echard privately fear that such an action, successful or not, would make a hero of its general and upset the council's balance of power. Zachareth is a close ally of Baron Greigory of Rhynn. It is whispered that Zachareth has fallen to the lure of sorcerous power, and he covets the hundreds of artifacts lost in the abandoned temples and castles of Roth's Vale — items that could be used to defeat the undead, or to raise and command them. His rune steed Backbreaker is rumored to be the work of a Runemaster's artifice. Sources The Riddles of the Runes (The Magic of Mennara), p. 117 Northern Terrinoth (Terrinoth), pp. 144–145 Roth's Vale (The Mistlands), p. 162

title: Zaff Darba
content: Zaff Darba Zaff Darba is a blade-laureate Sword Poet of Lorimor renowned for the masterwork Contemplations upon the Flametail, the most famous compilation of the deadly codas by which sword poets record their perfect killing blows. Sources Life in the West (Lorimor and the Torue Albes), p. 230

title: Zanaga
content: Zanaga Far to the southwest of Terrinoth lies the continent of Zanaga, where shadow-filled jungles hide ancient secrets from the sun and forbidding mountain peaks rise up to brood over a landscape unchanged since time began. Overview Here savage creatures dwell within the expansive wilderness, and proud tribes revere or resist them. In recent years, expeditions from other realms have pierced the jungle heart of this land, and fresh-cut settlements such as Herman's Gulch have risen along its rough trails and waterways. Though the invading torch of civilization has burnt away much of Zanaga's seemingly primitive darkness, many shadows remain, and many more secrets and wonders are yet to be discovered by those from across the sea. Heroes making the perilous ocean voyage to Zanaga will find a rich land of adventure and wealth before them, whether they wish to sign up with the Three Skulls Trading Company and forge trade routes into the interior, earn the respect of the Singhara and perhaps fight with them against Tarakhe's minions, set out on their own to uncover the lost empire of the Lizardmen, or battle the Nagas that dwell in their ruins. Sources Zanaga (Chapter III - Lands of Magic), p. 252

title: Zarihell
content: Zarihell Zarihell is an ancient Elf who roams The Mistlands at will, released — either mistakenly or unknowingly — when Timmorran rescued Waiqar from his imprisonment at Llovar's Black Citadel at the end of the First Darkness. She seems able to command the spirits of the living and dead alike with such power that she appears more bemused with Waiqar's efforts than fearful of them. Certain rumors suggest she was liberated from the Black Citadel's dungeons alongside Waiqar himself, though no official records confirm this; most agree only that she is an Elf of mysterious lineage and surpassing persuasive ability. During the Second Darkness, Zarihell established the first of the Death Cults of Waiqar in Tamalir, organizing cult activity across Terrinoth in coordination with Ardus Ix'Erebus's movement of the Deathborn Legion — though rumors have this as something she perhaps deigned to do more for her own benefit or amusement than out of loyalty to Waiqar. Sources The Second Darkness (Tales of Darkness), p. 41 Bilehall (The Mistlands), p. 161

title: Zir the Black
content: Zir the Black Zir the Black was one of the six dragonlords — alongside Margath, Baalesh, Levirax, Avox, and Gehennor — who each led a band of lesser drakes against a different part of the world during the Third Darkness, motivated by greed for the Stars of Timmorran. History According to some accounts, it was Zir who first discovered how to break Stars down into smaller fragments and inscribe runes upon them, using dragonfire to soften each Star and the incredible sharpness of her own claws to inscribe the mark — transforming the unstable Stars into stable runebound shards usable even by a bearer with no magical knowledge. Greyhaven's Runemasters suspect these carved runes are the dragons' own representations of the Yrthwrights' words; some are known as dragon runes, thought to incorporate the name of the dragonlord who inscribed them. This breakthrough transformed Margath's host from a formidable army into one nigh unbeatable, and Zir's own battered force of drakes and hybrids roamed the wilds of Terrinoth in the war's final year, hiding alongside their stolen hoard of treasure until Orc scouts found her body and those of hundreds of lesser Dragonkin, torn apart and burned — the suspected judgment of the Great Dragon Rex Shaarina upon dragonlords who had acted without her sanction. Sources The Third Darkness (Tales of Darkness), pp. 45–48

title: Zorgas
content: Zorgas Zorgas is Waiqar's grand holdfast, a black fortress at the heart of The Mistlands, said to have been built in the image of Llovar's Black Citadel. Zorgas lies at the center of a nigh-impassable bog whose terrain constantly shifts, clearing a path only when Waiqar himself wishes to ride out with his host. It is here that the most terrible of Waiqar's forces ready themselves for conquest: armies of Reanimates crew the parapets without rest, while the most favored of Waiqar's Deathborn sit at his Black Table, a grim mockery of the Council of Barons in Archaut. Warrens bored into the surrounding cliffsides house barrow wyrms, while the fortress's expansive dungeons hold Wraiths, banshees, and frenzied bone constructs too destructive to be allowed loose except when the utter annihilation of entire battlefields is desired. Tales also tell of the treasures found here: magical items and weapons of rarity and power dating from the First Darkness. Many of Greyhaven's scholars suspect untold numbers of runebound shards are locked away in Zorgas as well, in partial fulfillment of Waiqar's vow to claim them all for himself. Some venture here for other reasons, such as scouting out the forces of undeath for worried Daqan Lords — that almost none return has only increased their concern. Sources Zorgas (The Mistlands), p. 160
